column2: My program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file that saves each pupil.
I know what a form, a control, a property and IntelliSense are.
My program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file that saves each pupil.
Solution Explorer lists my forms, double-clicking one opens the Design tab, and View Code opens the code tab.
The green Start arrow runs my program and the red square stops it.
Every chapter has the same shape, and the home page shows me my next job.
A chapter is a row of parts, each part is a few screens, and each screen has one job.
The big button at the bottom ticks a screen off and moves me on.
The home page lists every part in order, I tick what I have done, and I open the first part that is not ticked.
Three rules run through every chapter of this guide.
The guide shows the names Mr Gartland gave his controls, and I use the names I gave mine, found at the top of the Properties window.
When I type the first letters of a name, IntelliSense lists the names in my program and Tab finishes it.
I cannot copy code from the guide, I type it, and I read each line as I type it.
I have tried to copy a line and seen the guide refuse.
A red wiggly line means Visual Studio does not understand that line, and the Error List takes me to it.
Build Solution checks every line, and Build succeeded at the bottom left means I can run it.
I check my login form for its two boxes, the Login button, the star in the password box and the Login button's code.
This part puts the panel, the two boxes, the labels and the Login button on the login form, each with a name.
My login form has a panel holding two text boxes, a Login button and their labels, plus a title and a ? button.
I name a control by clicking it once and typing its name beside Name near the top of Properties.
Setting PasswordChar to a star on tbxPassword makes every letter typed in it show as a star.
This part types the code behind the Login button, so that it checks the username and password.
If the username is more than 15 letters, a message appears and both boxes are emptied.
If the username is more than 15 letters, a message appears and both boxes are emptied.
If the username and password are both right, a message appears, the login form hides and the data entry form opens.
If the details are anything else, a Login incorrect message appears and both boxes are emptied.
I run the program and try a long username, a wrong password, the right details and two empty boxes.
I check my data entry form for its five panels, their names, the Save and View Report buttons and the year group list.
This part shows the five panels of the data entry form, then you drag them on and name them.
The data entry form holds five panels: pupil details, three attempts, the quiz, the reaction test and the group.
I drag five panels onto the data entry form and give each one a name that starts with pnl.
This part puts the right controls inside each of the five panels, one panel per screen.
The pupil details panel holds a first name box, a surname box, a gender list, a year group list, an Enter button and a ? button.
The year group list and the gender list each hold their choices, typed one per line in Items.
The second panel holds three attempt boxes with labels, a Calculate Average button, a box for the average and a ? button.
The quiz panel and the test panel each hold a heading, a not taken yet label, a Take button and a ? button.
The group panel holds a heading, a box, a button and a ? button. Save Details, View Report, a title and a logo sit on the form.
Every panel name starts pnl, every text box tbx, every button btn and every drop-down list cbx. None is a made-up name.
